yaml.title: CAA 2026 · Alligator
yaml.subtitle: From seriation output to a chronological knowledge graph

markdown.markdown:
This site accompanies a CAA 2026 contribution on modelling the chronology of
Arretine ware (*terra sigillata*) findspots in the north-western Roman
provinces. A Python pipeline reads the output of the
[Alligator](https://archaeology.link/) seriation tool, merges it with findspot
data, and produces a standards-compliant RDF knowledge graph together with a
set of figures.


The graph describes 45 findspots and their dating, and groups them in two
different ways.

| | Period cluster | Chronological horizon |
|---|---|---|
| Class | `lado:PeriodCluster` | `lado:ChronologicalHorizon`, `crm:E4_Period` |
| Origin | computed — findspots sharing an identical start and end year | interpretive — the phase a findspot was assigned to |
| Count | 8 | 5 |

Both groupings carry OWL-Time intervals and the full set of Allen relations
between them, so the same temporal reasoning can be applied to either. The
vocabularies used are CIDOC-CRM, OWL-Time, GeoSPARQL, SKOS and LADO, with
findspots linked to Wikidata and Pleiades.

[Download the graph (Turtle, ~2,000 triples)](notebook/arretine_sites_minigraph.ttl)

## Interactive notebook

The notebook below asks which findspots were still in use at the time of the
*Clades Variana* in AD 9, and answers it three times over — by comparing dates
directly, by reasoning over period clusters, and by reasoning over
chronological horizons. It runs entirely in your browser: no installation, no
server, no account.

[Open the interactive notebook →](notebook/clades-variana-temporal-live.qmd)

A companion Jupyter notebook with the identical analysis for a local Python
environment is in the repository at `notebook/clades_variana_temporal.ipynb`.

## Reproducing the pipeline

The figures and the graph are regenerated by a single command from the
repository root:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python py/main.py
```

This runs the RDF pipeline first and the service-composition analysis second —
the order matters, because the first step clears the output directory. Every
figure is written as both a 300 dpi JPEG and a pure-vector SVG, and the output
is byte-reproducible: rebuilding without changing anything produces identical
files, so a diff appears only when something really changed.

---

*Repository: [leiza-scit/CAA2026-alligator](https://github.com/leiza-scit/CAA2026-alligator)
· Seriation: Alligator · Variance and quality measures following the RGZM
method (A. Mees).*
